claim: In the matching retail DLL, the two MatchRandom.Range overloads used by already-canonical damage logic are exact 30-byte wrappers with one shared structural pattern. MatchRandom.Range(Int32 min, Int32 max) (0x0600497B) increments static Int32 field randomCnt, calls MemberRef 0x0A0001EC named Range on TypeRef UnityEngine.Random with min and max unchanged, stores the returned Int32 in lastRandNum_Int, reloads that field, and returns it. MatchRandom.Range(Float32 min, Float32 max) (0x0600497C) performs the same randomCnt increment, calls MemberRef 0x0A000804 named Range on TypeRef UnityEngine.Random with the two Float32 arguments unchanged, stores the returned Float32 in lastRandNum_Float, reloads that field, and returns it. FACT-0025 pins the Int32 overload call at mRate100Check IL+0x0003 with raw arguments 0 and 100. FACT-0022 pins the Float32 overload call at CriticalCheck IL+0x0292 with raw arguments 0.0f and 1.0f.
